deep.reconstruction:
Context: This page belongs to a German draft, numbered by articles, on the arithmetic-geometric mean (AGM). The previous page ends art. 3/4 with the identification M x = sqrt(x^2-1)/phi(sqrt(x^2/(x^2-1))). The forward AGM step is a' = (a+b)/2, b' = sqrt(ab), producing series I: a, a', a'', ... and series II: b, b', b'', .... This page extends both series to the LEFT, i.e. it inverts the AGM step.

(Art. 4, continued) Given a > b > 0, we want the pair ('a, 'b) whose arithmetic mean is a and whose geometric mean is b. So 'a + 'b = 2a and 'a·'b = b^2. Hence 'a and 'b are the roots of x^2 - 2a x + b^2 = 0, that is
  'a = a + sqrt(a^2 - b^2), 'b = a - sqrt(a^2 - b^2) [explicit formulas mine; the text only names the quadratic].
The larger root is taken as the term of I before a, and the smaller as the term of II before b. Iterating gives ''a, ''b as roots of x^2 - 2'a x + 'b'b = 0, then '''a, '''b as roots of x^2 - 2''a x + ''b''b = 0, and so on. Thus both series become two-sided infinite:
  ... IVa, '''a, ''a, 'a, a, a', a'', a''', aIV ... [I]
  ... IVb, '''b, ''b, 'b, b, b', b'', b''', bIV ... [II]
The backward step is always possible with real values. Since a > b, the discriminant is positive. Both roots are positive, because their sum 2a and product b^2 are positive.

Art. 5.
(a) The right-hand limit of I and of II is the same for every starting pair along the chain. It is M(any corresponding pair), because the AGM is invariant under the step.
(b) Every term of I is greater than this limit, and every term of II is smaller. I increases strictly from right to left, and II increases strictly from left to right. Footnote: the trivial case where all terms are equal is excluded.
(c) Growth to the left: 'a - 'b = 2 sqrt(a^2 - b^2) = 2(a-b) sqrt((a+b)/(a-b)). Because sqrt((a+b)/(a-b)) > 1 for b > 0, we get 'a - 'b > 2(a-b).
(d) By induction [mine], (n)a - (n)b > 2^n (a-b). Since (n)b > 0, this gives (n)a > 2^n (a-b) → ∞. So series I grows without bound to the left; this is the 'leicht schliesst' step.

The next page continues: the products 'a'b, ''a''b, ... equal b^2, 'b^2, ... and decrease, so II tends to 0 on the left. It then gives the worked example a = 1, b = 0.2. The left values check: 'a = 1 + sqrt(0.96) = 1.9797958971 and 'b = 0.0202041029. The right values converge to M(1, 0.2) ≈ 0.5208016382.

In modern terms, the inverse step is the ascending Landen (Gauss) transformation. It is the AGM read backwards. Writing b = a·cos(phi) gives 'a - 'b = 2a·sin(phi), so the backward iteration roughly doubles the 'gap' each step.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
The phrase 'die Grössern ... als das Glied der Reihe I' slips grammatically (should be 'die grössere'); this is not mathematical.
The step from 'a-'b > 2(a-b) to unbounded growth of I tacitly uses (n)b > 0, so that (n)a > (n)a-(n)b > 2^n (a-b). This is correct but left implicit.
The claim that the inverse step is always real needs a > b at every stage. It holds because 'a > a > b > 'b; this is not stated but is true.

results.what: Inversion of the AGM step: the predecessors ('a, 'b) of (a, b) are the roots of x^2 - 2a x + b^2 = 0. This extends the AGM sequences to bi-infinite sequences.
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1784) and Landen (1775) for the transformations; Gauss for the AGM formulation (1791–1800)

results.what: Invariance of the AGM along the chain, and monotonicity: I decreases and II increases to the right, with I > M > II.
results.modern_name: Basic properties of the arithmetic-geometric mean

results.what: 'a - 'b = 2 sqrt(a^2-b^2) > 2(a-b), hence I → ∞ to the left. Products 'a'b = b^2 decrease, hence II → 0 to the left (completed on the next page).
results.modern_name: Divergence of the ascending Landen sequence (modulus → 1 direction)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, in his Nachlass treatise on AGM (Werke III)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a German draft of material Gauss treats in his posthumously published AGM papers (Werke III, 'De origine proprietatibusque generalibus numerorum mediorum arithm.-geometricorum'), where the two-sided extension of the series appears. It is elementary and already attributed to him.

'Die Grössern (im fall sie ungleich sind)': the manuscript reads 'die Grössere ... das Kleinere' (singular), roughly.
In '... zwischen zweien beliebigen [-?-] correspondirenden Gliedern' the struck item is a single cancelled character or word before 'correspondirenden'.
In 'da 'a - 'b = 2√(aa - bb)' the manuscript shows corrections: a '±' overwritten on '-' and the 'aa' partly rewritten. The intended reading is 'a - 'b = 2√(aa-bb).
